44	
45	The default run replays the shipped ledger and imports none of these. They are needed only to **record** a ledger (`--live`) or to run a local model.
46	
47	| Package | Pin | Used for |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| **openai** | 3.51.0 | OpenAI (`openai:` or `openai-chat:`) **and** the local Ollama model (`ollama:`). Already installed in the spike venv. |
50	| **google-genai** | pin on the day (library requires `>=2.30,<3`) | Gemini (`google:`), via `pydantic-ai-slim[google]` |
51	| **anthropic** | 2.9.0 | Claude (`anthropic:`), optional |
52	
53	### Dev only (`requirements-dev.txt`)
54	
55	| Package | Pin | Used for |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| **pytest** | 9.2.0 | Unit, perturbation, red-team and eval tests |
58	| **hypothesis** | 6.170.15 | Property tests over random input changes: balance sheet always balances, IC always nets to zero, both reserve routes always agree. This is what exposes a hardcoded constant. |
59	| **pydantic-evals** | 2.68.0 | The eval harness for the AI layer (cases, evaluators, reports) so recall, false positives and injection invariance are measured the same way every time. Wave 3. |
60	| **ruff** | 0.17.5 | Lint and format, one tool |
61	| **mypy** | 2.4.1 | Static types on `core/` and `types.py`, where a type slip becomes a wrong number |
62	
63	## 3. The LLM layer: provider-neutral rules, and provider notes
64	
65	The code is provider-neutral: the model is a config string (`ollama:`, `openai:`, `google:`, `anthropic:`) and everything else is the same. What follows are rules that hold for **any** provider, then what is known per provider.
66	
67	### Rules that hold for every provider
68	| Topic | Rule | Why |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| Model choice | Chosen by the **eval set**, not by name or reputation | The labelled units decide accuracy, false alarms, speed and cost |
71	| Determinism | Comes only from the **ledger replay**, never from sampling settings | Some current models reject `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` or `seed`; the local model is not repeatable even at temperature 0 |
72	| Sampling and reasoning settings | Live in `config/llm.toml` and are sent **only if the provider accepts them** | A rejected parameter must not break a run |
73	| Output | Structured output validated by Pydantic (`NativeOutput`), one model per unit type, **booleans not lists**, risk derived in code | Small and large models both degrade on list fields in constrained decoding |
74	| Tools | None | The reviewer cannot act, only answer |
75	| Refusals and stop reasons | Check the stop reason before reading content; record a refusal as "no finding, refused" in the ledger and surface it as an issue | Providers can decline with HTTP 200 |
76	| Retries | The SDK retries transient errors; our graph retries **only grounding failures**, once | Two different things |
77	| Credentials | Environment variable per provider, never in the repo or a transcript | Table in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` section 1 |
78	
79	### Provider notes (and how each was verified)
80	| Provider | What is known | Verified |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| **Ollama, local** | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` works through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint; see section 8 | Live, on this machine |
83	| **Claude** | Current models reject sampling parameters and forced tool choice; thinking is always on and depth is set with effort (default `medium` on Opus 5.5). Structured output via `output_config` / `NativeOutput`. | Read from the current Claude API documentation and the library's profile; **not called live** |
84	| **OpenAI** | `openai:` uses the Responses API model class, `openai-chat:` the chat class; the library flags that some models do not allow sampling parameters | Read from library source; **first live call tomorrow** |
85	| **Gemini** | `google:` model class with native structured output; key `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (legacy `GEMINI_API_KEY`) | Read from library source; **first live call tomorrow** |
86	
87	## 3b. Config format: TOML, not YAML (found by test)
88	
89	| Input | YAML (PyYAML `safe_load`) | TOML (stdlib `tomllib`) |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| `[0030, 0031, 7100]` (UK plant codes) | silently becomes `[24, 25, 7100]` (octal) | **error**: unquoted leading zero is refused |
92	| `"0031"` quoted | string | string |
93	| `rate: 1.2530` | float `1.253` | quote it as a string, read as `Decimal` |
94	| `no` / `NO` | `False` | plain strings stay strings |
95	
96	YAML would reproduce exactly the leading-zero trap in this bundle, inside our own config. TOML is stricter, has comments, is readable by hand, and is in the standard library, so **PyYAML is dropped as a dependency**. Rates and amounts in config are written as quoted strings and parsed to `Decimal`.
97	
98	## 3c. PydanticAI: where it sits and what it is used for
99	
100	Decision: **LangGraph orchestrates the workflow; PydanticAI is the model-calling harness inside the AI nodes only.** (Your suggestion, accepted with boundaries. My earlier objection was "an extra layer over one call"; the reasons below outweigh it.)
101	
102	| Capability | Why we use it | Checked |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| **Model switch by config** (`ollama:...` now, `openai:...` or `google:...` tomorrow, `anthropic:...` optional, `test`) | Same code runs on a local model, any cloud model, or offline | Yes, with `test`; local model run live; cloud providers tomorrow |
105	| **Typed structured output**, validated by Pydantic, one model per unit type (`NativeOutput(MappingVerdict)`) | Output can only be a schema-valid object | Yes |
106	| **Retry on invalid output** (`retries=`) | Our bounded retry for malformed AI output | Yes (bad answer, then good: 2 model calls) |
107	| **Claude forced-tool-choice restriction** (only if Claude is used) | The library's Anthropic profile lists `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` as rejecting forced tool choice and falls back for its own output tool | Read in source. Not tested live (no key). |
108	| **Ledger replay** with a `FunctionModel` that answers from `ledger/<model>.jsonl` | A ledger miss raises, so there is never a silent API call | Yes: replay identical to recorded; miss raises |
109	| **Offline tests** | `FunctionModel` (works with `NativeOutput`); `TestModel` works only in tool-output mode | Yes |
110	| **Local models** through the OpenAI-compatible Ollama provider | See section 8 | Yes |
111	| Usage limits, OpenTelemetry, MCP client and toolsets, `pydantic-evals` | Request caps; optional tracing (off); optional read-only "fetch more context" tools (designed); the eval harness (Wave 3) | Not yet |
112	
113	**Boundaries:**
114	- Only one adapter module, `llm/`, imports `pydantic_ai`, so a v2 API change touches one file. (Already seen: `result.usage` became a property.)
115	- No agent calls another agent. No tools by default. `UsageLimits(request_limit=2)` on every run.
116	- **No telemetry leaves the machine.** Logfire is not configured, and `PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER=1` is set. The only outbound traffic is the model call, and only in `--live`.
117	- Thinking and effort go through `model_settings`, and the ledger records them in the key.
118	- Footprint: about 12 extra packages (60 to 72 in the test venv).
119	
120	## 4. Verified on this machine (spike)
121	
122	| Check | Result |
123	|---|---|
124	| Clean venv, exact pins installed | **Pass**, 60 packages (this set included PyYAML, which is no longer needed), pip 26.3 inside the venv |
125	| LangGraph interrupt, then resume **in a separate process** from the SQLite checkpoint | **Pass** |
126	| `Decimal("1234567.891234567891")` stored in graph state, round-tripped through the checkpoint | **Pass**, exact value and type preserved |
127	| Installed `anthropic` exposes `messages.parse(output_format=...)` | **Pass** |
128	
129	Not verified: a real API call (no key supplied yet), an install on Linux or macOS, Python 3.12 / 3.13.
130	
131	**Effect on a design claim:** v2 said state carries pointers because `Decimal` might not survive checkpointing. It does survive. Pointer-state stays, but the reasons are now size, an auditable store of record, and one place for exact queries, not a serialisation risk.
132	
133	## 5. Deliberately not used
134	
135	| Candidate | Why not |
136	|---|---|
137	| pandas / numpy | Float defaults are a correctness risk for money, and the data is small. `csv` + `Decimal` is exact and explainable line by line. |
138	| LangChain (beyond what LangGraph pulls in) | Not needed. We call one SDK directly. |
139	| Vector database / embeddings | Design decision: exact structured joins, not similarity search. |
140	| **Langfuse** (LLM observability) | Self-hosting is a web service and a worker plus Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis and object storage; Docker is not installed here; the hosted version sends prompts off the machine; the ledger already records every call. Kept only as an optional OpenTelemetry target. |
141	| **DeepEval** (LLM evals) | Metrics are LLM-as-judge by default (OpenAI unless configured) and need a key; it has opt-out telemetry (`DEEPEVAL_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT=1`). Our units have ground truth, so deterministic evaluators in `pydantic-evals` are stricter and cheaper. |
142	| MongoDB or the Cosmos DB emulator | Both need a running service (the emulator is Windows or Docker based). Docker and `mongod` are **not installed** on this machine, and a reviewer would have to install a server before `python run.py consolidate` works. Our core data is relational (rows joined by exact keys, summed, traced), which a document store does worse. The document-shaped parts (AI ledger, findings) are handled by **SQLite JSON** (`json_extract`, a `json_valid` check constraint, expression indexes), verified here on SQLite 3.38.4. |
143	| SQLAlchemy | `sqlite3` with a handful of tables is enough. |
144	| Typer / Click | `argparse` covers seven subcommands and has no install. |
145	| Streamlit or any UI | The UI is designed, not built. A thin review page is a last-hours extra only if everything else is done. |
146	| Docker | A fresh-clone `venv` run is what they will do. A container adds a layer between them and the code. |
147	| uv | Not installed here, and pip-compatible requirements files already work with it for anyone who prefers it. |
148	
149	## 6. Open items
150	
151	1. **Which cloud provider tomorrow, OpenAI or Gemini?** Either works through the same config. The eval decides the model.
152	2. **CI.** A small GitHub Actions workflow (pytest on Windows and Linux) shows fresh-clone reproducibility. Planned for Wave 2.
153	3. **Pins for the cloud SDKs** are fixed on the day they are first installed.
154	
155	## 7. Storage behind an interface, and the product database
156	
157	All storage goes through one small module (`store.py`) with a handful of operations (put ledger call, get by key, write finding, read facts, exact joins for lineage). SQLite is the implementation in the prototype. **In the product the database would be PostgreSQL**: relational tables for ledger lines and lineage, `JSONB` columns for AI calls and findings (so documents and relations live in one transactional store), append-only audit tables enforced by constraints, and row-level security for tenant isolation. A document database such as MongoDB or Cosmos DB would only earn its place for storing very heterogeneous raw ERP payloads at scale, and even that fits in `JSONB`. This is a `DECISIONS.md` entry: *storage engine, options considered: committed text only, SQLite, Mongo/Cosmos, Postgres*.
158	
159	## 8. Local model evaluation (Ollama, this machine)
160	
161	**Hardware:** RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, 4 GB VRAM, 15 GB RAM, on AC power in the Performance plan. The display runs on the AMD Radeon integrated GPU; the NVIDIA card is used on demand.
162	
163	### Who uses the GPU
164	- **NVIDIA total in use: 657 to 850 MiB** with all your normal apps open (132 MiB of that is driver-reserved), leaving about **3.2 GB free**.
165	- Windows will not attribute VRAM per process on this card (`nvidia-smi` shows N/A under the Windows display driver model), so per-process figures are a **relative ranking only**: the desktop compositor (`dwm`) is largest, then Excel, then small amounts from Explorer, Claude, Edge WebView2, Antigravity IDE, Copilot, Teams, WhatsApp, Radeon Software. About 25 processes hold a GPU context.
166	- **Nothing had to be closed.** The earlier slowness (9 tokens/s, half the model on the CPU) happened when about 1.5 GB was already in use. With 3.2 GB free, a 4B model fits fully on the GPU.
167	
168	### Models tested (same 21 labelled units from the real bundle, temperature 0, seed 7, 400-token cap, schema-constrained output through PydanticAI)
169	
170	| Model | On GPU | Generation speed | Result on 21 units |
171	|---|---|---|---|
172	| **qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M** (2.5 GB) | 100% (3.0 to 3.2 GB) | **22 to 24 tok/s**, median 7.5 s per unit, 183 s for all 21 | **20 / 21 correct, 21 / 21 schema-valid**, 0 false alarms on mappings, 1 false alarm (JE-010) |
173	| qwen3.5:4b (thinking family, thinking off) | 100% now (19 tok/s); half on CPU when VRAM was tight (9 tok/s) | 19 tok/s | 16 / 21; 5 of 13 clean units flagged; thinking on is unusable (447 s, then failed) |
174	| phi4-mini 3.8b (2.5 GB) | 100% | 24 tok/s | **Rejected:** 8 of its first 11 units wrong (flagged correct mappings), then stalled |
175	
176	### What affects speed and fit
177	| Lever | Effect |
178	|---|---|
179	| Free VRAM before loading | **Decisive**: fit or half-CPU is a 2x speed difference |
180	| Smaller `num_ctx` (2048 / 3072 / 4096) | Inconsistent fit results across runs; not a reliable lever |
181	| Flash attention + 8-bit KV cache (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`) | Same speed, but **2.9 GB instead of 3.2 GB**, so more headroom against other apps |
182	| Schema-constrained vs free JSON; CPU thread count | **No effect** (22.7 tok/s in every case; CPU idle) |
183	| "Keep the reason to 20 words" | 2.1x faster per unit (3.5 s) but **accuracy fell from 20/21 to 16/21**: the explanation helps the model. Do not shorten. |
184	| GPU clocks | Reaches its 6001 MHz memory clock and 1500 MHz core clock under load. Not stuck in a low power state. |
185	
186	**Ceiling: about 23 tokens/s for a 4B model on this card.** Faster needs a smaller model (a 1.7B download was started and cut off by the restart; not tested) or fewer output tokens. An 8B model (5.2 GB) cannot fit.
187	
188	### The finding that changes the design
189	**Not repeatable, even at temperature 0 with a fixed seed.** Run twice, `qwen3:4b-instruct` gave a different decision on 1 of 4 units: for JE-006 (the injection case) run 2 returned a degenerate repeated category list and `risk: false` while still listing "unbalanced". (`qwen3.5:4b` was identical on 3 of 3 units, so it varies by model.)
190	
191	Consequences, now part of the design:
192	1. **The ledger is the only source of determinism.** A local model can never be re-run to reproduce a result.
193	2. **Use one boolean per risk category, not a list.** Lists degenerate in constrained decoding.
194	3. **Derive `risk` in code** from the booleans. The model must not be able to say `risk: false` while flagging a category.
195	4. **The grounding verifier checks every claim separately**: for example "unbalanced" is checked against the actual debits and credits, and "exceeds balance" against the actual balance.
196	5. Keep the prompt version in the ledger key: small models are sensitive to wording.
197	
198	### Verdict
199	`qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` is a usable **free, offline second opinion for the scoped unit review (L3), behind the grounding verifier**: fast enough for a one-time recording run (about 100 units in 10 to 15 minutes), accurate on this set, and zero-cost. It is **not** the primary reviewer, not interactive, and not for long-context jobs. Sample size is small (21 units, my labels), so treat the numbers as indicative.
200	
201	**Where it earns its place:** development and the eval harness without an API key; live-session resilience (a changed input that misses the ledger can be answered on your laptop with no internet); and **model diversity** (a cloud model and a different-family local model agreeing is a stronger independent signal). The shipped ledger is recorded with the cloud model the eval selects.
202	
203	**Recommended local settings:** `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, `num_ctx` 4096, `num_predict` 400, temperature 0, fixed seed, full-length reasons.
204	
205	### Housekeeping
206	`phi4-mini` was rejected and removed. Installed now: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` (recommended) and your original `qwen3.5:4b`. The interrupted `qwen3:1.7b` download left a small partial file; that model was not tested.
207	
208	## 9. Logging, tracing and evals (decision)
209	
210	- **Audit lineage** is an output of the engine (origin rows, traces, manifest), not a tool. See `ARCHITECTURE_v2.md` section 16.
211	- **Run log:** stdlib `logging`, JSON lines per run in `.northwind/logs/`. No logging framework.
212	- **LLM observability:** the ledger. Optional OpenTelemetry export via PydanticAI instrumentation, off by default. The installed set contains only the OpenTelemetry **API**, with no exporter, so nothing leaves the machine unless an SDK and exporter are added deliberately.
213	- **Evals:** `pydantic-evals` (already pinned) with custom deterministic evaluators, run under pytest. An LLM-judge evaluator exists in the same package if narration ever needs one.
214

| **openai** | 3.51.0 | OpenAI (`openai:` or `openai-chat:`) **and** the local Ollama model (`ollama:`). Already installed in the spike venv. |
| **google-genai** | pin on the day (library requires `>=2.30,<3`) | Gemini (`google:`), via `pydantic-ai-slim[google]` |
| **anthropic** | 2.9.0 | Claude (`anthropic:`), optional |

### Dev only (`requirements-dev.txt`)

| Package | Pin | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **pytest** | 9.2.0 | Unit, perturbation, red-team and eval tests |
| **hypothesis** | 6.170.15 | Property tests over random input changes: balance sheet always balances, IC always nets to zero, both reserve routes always agree. This is what exposes a hardcoded constant. |
| **pydantic-evals** | 2.68.0 | The eval harness for the AI layer (cases, evaluators, reports) so recall, false positives and injection invariance are measured the same way every time. Wave 3. |
| **ruff** | 0.17.5 | Lint and format, one tool |
| **mypy** | 2.4.1 | Static types on `core/` and `types.py`, where a type slip becomes a wrong number |

## 3. The LLM layer: provider-neutral rules, and provider notes

The code is provider-neutral: the model is a config string (`ollama:`, `openai:`, `google:`, `anthropic:`) and everything else is the same. What follows are rules that hold for **any** provider, then what is known per provider.

### Rules that hold for every provider
| Topic | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Model choice | Chosen by the **eval set**, not by name or reputation | The labelled units decide accuracy, false alarms, speed and cost |
| Determinism | Comes only from the **ledger replay**, never from sampling settings | Some current models reject `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` or `seed`; the local model is not repeatable even at temperature 0 |
| Sampling and reasoning settings | Live in `config/llm.toml` and are sent **only if the provider accepts them** | A rejected parameter must not break a run |
| Output | Structured output validated by Pydantic (`NativeOutput`), one model per unit type, **booleans not lists**, risk derived in code | Small and large models both degrade on list fields in constrained decoding |
| Tools | None | The reviewer cannot act, only answer |
| Refusals and stop reasons | Check the stop reason before reading content; record a refusal as "no finding, refused" in the ledger and surface it as an issue | Providers can decline with HTTP 200 |
| Retries | The SDK retries transient errors; our graph retries **only grounding failures**, once | Two different things |
| Credentials | Environment variable per provider, never in the repo or a transcript | Table in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` section 1 |

### Provider notes (and how each was verified)
| Provider | What is known | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| **Ollama, local** | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` works through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint; see section 8 | Live, on this machine |
| **Claude** | Current models reject sampling parameters and forced tool choice; thinking is always on and depth is set with effort (default `medium` on Opus 5.5). Structured output via `output_config` / `NativeOutput`. | Read from the current Claude API documentation and the library's profile; **not called live** |
| **OpenAI** | `openai:` uses the Responses API model class, `openai-chat:` the chat class; the library flags that some models do not allow sampling parameters | Read from library source; **first live call tomorrow** |
| **Gemini** | `google:` model class with native structured output; key `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (legacy `GEMINI_API_KEY`) | Read from library source; **first live call tomorrow** |

## 3b. Config format: TOML, not YAML (found by test)

| Input | YAML (PyYAML `safe_load`) | TOML (stdlib `tomllib`) |
|---|---|---|
| `[0030, 0031, 7100]` (UK plant codes) | silently becomes `[24, 25, 7100]` (octal) | **error**: unquoted leading zero is refused |
| `"0031"` quoted | string | string |
| `rate: 1.2530` | float `1.253` | quote it as a string, read as `Decimal` |
| `no` / `NO` | `False` | plain strings stay strings |

YAML would reproduce exactly the leading-zero trap in this bundle, inside our own config. TOML is stricter, has comments, is readable by hand, and is in the standard library, so **PyYAML is dropped as a dependency**. Rates and amounts in config are written as quoted strings and parsed to `Decimal`.

## 3c. PydanticAI: where it sits and what it is used for

Decision: **LangGraph orchestrates the workflow; PydanticAI is the model-calling harness inside the AI nodes only.** (Your suggestion, accepted with boundaries. My earlier objection was "an extra layer over one call"; the reasons below outweigh it.)

| Capability | Why we use it | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| **Model switch by config** (`ollama:...` now, `openai:...` or `google:...` tomorrow, `anthropic:...` optional, `test`) | Same code runs on a local model, any cloud model, or offline | Yes, with `test`; local model run live; cloud providers tomorrow |
| **Typed structured output**, validated by Pydantic, one model per unit type (`NativeOutput(MappingVerdict)`) | Output can only be a schema-valid object | Yes |
| **Retry on invalid output** (`retries=`) | Our bounded retry for malformed AI output | Yes (bad answer, then good: 2 model calls) |
| **Claude forced-tool-choice restriction** (only if Claude is used) | The library's Anthropic profile lists `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` as rejecting forced tool choice and falls back for its own output tool | Read in source. Not tested live (no key). |
| **Ledger replay** with a `FunctionModel` that answers from `ledger/<model>.jsonl` | A ledger miss raises, so there is never a silent API call | Yes: replay identical to recorded; miss raises |
| **Offline tests** | `FunctionModel` (works with `NativeOutput`); `TestModel` works only in tool-output mode | Yes |
| **Local models** through the OpenAI-compatible Ollama provider | See section 8 | Yes |
| Usage limits, OpenTelemetry, MCP client and toolsets, `pydantic-evals` | Request caps; optional tracing (off); optional read-only "fetch more context" tools (designed); the eval harness (Wave 3) | Not yet |

**Boundaries:**
- Only one adapter module, `llm/`, imports `pydantic_ai`, so a v2 API change touches one file. (Already seen: `result.usage` became a property.)
- No agent calls another agent. No tools by default. `UsageLimits(request_limit=2)` on every run.
- **No telemetry leaves the machine.** Logfire is not configured, and `PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER=1` is set. The only outbound traffic is the model call, and only in `--live`.
- Thinking and effort go through `model_settings`, and the ledger records them in the key.
- Footprint: about 12 extra packages (60 to 72 in the test venv).

## 4. Verified on this machine (spike)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Clean venv, exact pins installed | **Pass**, 60 packages (this set included PyYAML, which is no longer needed), pip 26.3 inside the venv |
| LangGraph interrupt, then resume **in a separate process** from the SQLite checkpoint | **Pass** |
| `Decimal("1234567.891234567891")` stored in graph state, round-tripped through the checkpoint | **Pass**, exact value and type preserved |
| Installed `anthropic` exposes `messages.parse(output_format=...)` | **Pass** |

Not verified: a real API call (no key supplied yet), an install on Linux or macOS, Python 3.12 / 3.13.

**Effect on a design claim:** v2 said state carries pointers because `Decimal` might not survive checkpointing. It does survive. Pointer-state stays, but the reasons are now size, an auditable store of record, and one place for exact queries, not a serialisation risk.

## 5. Deliberately not used

| Candidate | Why not |
|---|---|
| pandas / numpy | Float defaults are a correctness risk for money, and the data is small. `csv` + `Decimal` is exact and explainable line by line. |
| LangChain (beyond what LangGraph pulls in) | Not needed. We call one SDK directly. |
| Vector database / embeddings | Design decision: exact structured joins, not similarity search. |
| **Langfuse** (LLM observability) | Self-hosting is a web service and a worker plus Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis and object storage; Docker is not installed here; the hosted version sends prompts off the machine; the ledger already records every call. Kept only as an optional OpenTelemetry target. |
| **DeepEval** (LLM evals) | Metrics are LLM-as-judge by default (OpenAI unless configured) and need a key; it has opt-out telemetry (`DEEPEVAL_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT=1`). Our units have ground truth, so deterministic evaluators in `pydantic-evals` are stricter and cheaper. |
| MongoDB or the Cosmos DB emulator | Both need a running service (the emulator is Windows or Docker based). Docker and `mongod` are **not installed** on this machine, and a reviewer would have to install a server before `python run.py consolidate` works. Our core data is relational (rows joined by exact keys, summed, traced), which a document store does worse. The document-shaped parts (AI ledger, findings) are handled by **SQLite JSON** (`json_extract`, a `json_valid` check constraint, expression indexes), verified here on SQLite 3.38.4. |
| SQLAlchemy | `sqlite3` with a handful of tables is enough. |
| Typer / Click | `argparse` covers seven subcommands and has no install. |
| Streamlit or any UI | The UI is designed, not built. A thin review page is a last-hours extra only if everything else is done. |
| Docker | A fresh-clone `venv` run is what they will do. A container adds a layer between them and the code. |
| uv | Not installed here, and pip-compatible requirements files already work with it for anyone who prefers it. |

## 6. Open items

1. **Which cloud provider tomorrow, OpenAI or Gemini?** Either works through the same config. The eval decides the model.
2. **CI.** A small GitHub Actions workflow (pytest on Windows and Linux) shows fresh-clone reproducibility. Planned for Wave 2.
3. **Pins for the cloud SDKs** are fixed on the day they are first installed.

## 7. Storage behind an interface, and the product database

All storage goes through one small module (`store.py`) with a handful of operations (put ledger call, get by key, write finding, read facts, exact joins for lineage). SQLite is the implementation in the prototype. **In the product the database would be PostgreSQL**: relational tables for ledger lines and lineage, `JSONB` columns for AI calls and findings (so documents and relations live in one transactional store), append-only audit tables enforced by constraints, and row-level security for tenant isolation. A document database such as MongoDB or Cosmos DB would only earn its place for storing very heterogeneous raw ERP payloads at scale, and even that fits in `JSONB`. This is a `DECISIONS.md` entry: *storage engine, options considered: committed text only, SQLite, Mongo/Cosmos, Postgres*.

## 8. Local model evaluation (Ollama, this machine)

**Hardware:** RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, 4 GB VRAM, 15 GB RAM, on AC power in the Performance plan. The display runs on the AMD Radeon integrated GPU; the NVIDIA card is used on demand.

### Who uses the GPU
- **NVIDIA total in use: 657 to 850 MiB** with all your normal apps open (132 MiB of that is driver-reserved), leaving about **3.2 GB free**.
- Windows will not attribute VRAM per process on this card (`nvidia-smi` shows N/A under the Windows display driver model), so per-process figures are a **relative ranking only**: the desktop compositor (`dwm`) is largest, then Excel, then small amounts from Explorer, Claude, Edge WebView2, Antigravity IDE, Copilot, Teams, WhatsApp, Radeon Software. About 25 processes hold a GPU context.
- **Nothing had to be closed.** The earlier slowness (9 tokens/s, half the model on the CPU) happened when about 1.5 GB was already in use. With 3.2 GB free, a 4B model fits fully on the GPU.

### Models tested (same 21 labelled units from the real bundle, temperature 0, seed 7, 400-token cap, schema-constrained output through PydanticAI)

| Model | On GPU | Generation speed | Result on 21 units |
|---|---|---|---|
| **qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M** (2.5 GB) | 100% (3.0 to 3.2 GB) | **22 to 24 tok/s**, median 7.5 s per unit, 183 s for all 21 | **20 / 21 correct, 21 / 21 schema-valid**, 0 false alarms on mappings, 1 false alarm (JE-010) |
| qwen3.5:4b (thinking family, thinking off) | 100% now (19 tok/s); half on CPU when VRAM was tight (9 tok/s) | 19 tok/s | 16 / 21; 5 of 13 clean units flagged; thinking on is unusable (447 s, then failed) |
| phi4-mini 3.8b (2.5 GB) | 100% | 24 tok/s | **Rejected:** 8 of its first 11 units wrong (flagged correct mappings), then stalled |

### What affects speed and fit
| Lever | Effect |
|---|---|
| Free VRAM before loading | **Decisive**: fit or half-CPU is a 2x speed difference |
| Smaller `num_ctx` (2048 / 3072 / 4096) | Inconsistent fit results across runs; not a reliable lever |
| Flash attention + 8-bit KV cache (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`) | Same speed, but **2.9 GB instead of 3.2 GB**, so more headroom against other apps |
| Schema-constrained vs free JSON; CPU thread count | **No effect** (22.7 tok/s in every case; CPU idle) |
| "Keep the reason to 20 words" | 2.1x faster per unit (3.5 s) but **accuracy fell from 20/21 to 16/21**: the explanation helps the model. Do not shorten. |
| GPU clocks | Reaches its 6001 MHz memory clock and 1500 MHz core clock under load. Not stuck in a low power state. |

**Ceiling: about 23 tokens/s for a 4B model on this card.** Faster needs a smaller model (a 1.7B download was started and cut off by the restart; not tested) or fewer output tokens. An 8B model (5.2 GB) cannot fit.

### The finding that changes the design
**Not repeatable, even at temperature 0 with a fixed seed.** Run twice, `qwen3:4b-instruct` gave a different decision on 1 of 4 units: for JE-006 (the injection case) run 2 returned a degenerate repeated category list and `risk: false` while still listing "unbalanced". (`qwen3.5:4b` was identical on 3 of 3 units, so it varies by model.)

Consequences, now part of the design:
1. **The ledger is the only source of determinism.** A local model can never be re-run to reproduce a result.
2. **Use one boolean per risk category, not a list.** Lists degenerate in constrained decoding.
3. **Derive `risk` in code** from the booleans. The model must not be able to say `risk: false` while flagging a category.
4. **The grounding verifier checks every claim separately**: for example "unbalanced" is checked against the actual debits and credits, and "exceeds balance" against the actual balance.
5. Keep the prompt version in the ledger key: small models are sensitive to wording.

### Verdict
`qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` is a usable **free, offline second opinion for the scoped unit review (L3), behind the grounding verifier**: fast enough for a one-time recording run (about 100 units in 10 to 15 minutes), accurate on this set, and zero-cost. It is **not** the primary reviewer, not interactive, and not for long-context jobs. Sample size is small (21 units, my labels), so treat the numbers as indicative.

**Where it earns its place:** development and the eval harness without an API key; live-session resilience (a changed input that misses the ledger can be answered on your laptop with no internet); and **model diversity** (a cloud model and a different-family local model agreeing is a stronger independent signal). The shipped ledger is recorded with the cloud model the eval selects.

**Recommended local settings:** `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, `num_ctx` 4096, `num_predict` 400, temperature 0, fixed seed, full-length reasons.

### Housekeeping
`phi4-mini` was rejected and removed. Installed now: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` (recommended) and your original `qwen3.5:4b`. The interrupted `qwen3:1.7b` download left a small partial file; that model was not tested.

## 9. Logging, tracing and evals (decision)

- **Audit lineage** is an output of the engine (origin rows, traces, manifest), not a tool. See `ARCHITECTURE_v2.md` section 16.
- **Run log:** stdlib `logging`, JSON lines per run in `.northwind/logs/`. No logging framework.
- **LLM observability:** the ledger. Optional OpenTelemetry export via PydanticAI instrumentation, off by default. The installed set contains only the OpenTelemetry **API**, with no exporter, so nothing leaves the machine unless an SDK and exporter are added deliberately.
- **Evals:** `pydantic-evals` (already pinned) with custom deterministic evaluators, run under pytest. An LLM-judge evaluator exists in the same package if narration ever needs one.

63	## 3. The LLM layer: provider-neutral rules, and provider notes
64	
65	The code is provider-neutral: the model is a config string (`ollama:`, `openai:`, `google:`, `anthropic:`) and everything else is the same. What follows are rules that hold for **any** provider, then what is known per provider.

67	### Rules that hold for every provider
68	| Topic | Rule | Why |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| Model choice | Chosen by the **eval set**, not by name or reputation | The labelled units decide accuracy, false alarms, speed and cost |
71	| Determinism | Comes only from the **ledger replay**, never from sampling settings | Some current models reject `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` or `seed`; the local model is not repeatable even at temperature 0 |
72	| Sampling and reasoning settings | Live in `config/llm.toml` and are sent **only if the provider accepts them** | A rejected parameter must not break a run |
73	| Output | Structured output validated by Pydantic (`NativeOutput`), one model per unit type, **booleans not lists**, risk derived in code | Small and large models both degrade on list fields in constrained decoding |
74	| Tools | None | The reviewer cannot act, only answer |
75	| Refusals and stop reasons | Check the stop reason before reading content; record a refusal as "no finding, refused" in the ledger and surface it as an issue | Providers can decline with HTTP 200 |
76	| Retries | The SDK retries transient errors; our graph retries **only grounding failures**, once | Two different things |
77	| Credentials | Environment variable per provider, never in the repo or a transcript | Table in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` section 1 |

87	## 3b. Config format: TOML, not YAML (found by test)
88	
89	| Input | YAML (PyYAML `safe_load`) | TOML (stdlib `tomllib`) |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| `[0030, 0031, 7100]` (UK plant codes) | silently becomes `[24, 25, 7100]` (octal) | **error**: unquoted leading zero is refused |

94	| `no` / `NO` | `False` | plain strings stay strings |

96	YAML would reproduce exactly the leading-zero trap in this bundle, inside our own config. TOML is stricter, has comments, is readable by hand, and is in the standard library, so **PyYAML is dropped as a dependency**. Rates and amounts in config are written as quoted strings and parsed to `Decimal`.

155	## 7. Storage behind an interface, and the product database
156	
157	All storage goes through one small module (`store.py`) with a handful of operations (put ledger call, get by key, write finding, read facts, exact joins for lineage). SQLite is the implementation in the prototype. **In the product the database would be PostgreSQL**: relational tables for ledger lines and lineage, `JSONB` columns for AI calls and findings (so documents and relations live in one transactional store), append-only audit tables enforced by constraints, and row-level security for tenant isolation. A document database such as MongoDB or Cosmos DB would only earn its place for storing very heterogeneous raw ERP payloads at scale, and even that fits in `JSONB`. This is a `DECISIONS.md` entry: *storage engine, options considered: committed text only, SQLite, Mongo/Cosmos, Postgres*.

172	| **qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M** (2.5 GB) | 100% (3.0 to 3.2 GB) | **22 to 24 tok/s**, median 7.5 s per unit, 183 s for all 21 | **20 / 21 correct, 21 / 21 schema-valid**, 0 false alarms on mappings, 1 false alarm (JE-010) |
173	| qwen3.5:4b (thinking family, thinking off) | 100% now (19 tok/s); half on CPU when VRAM was tight (9 tok/s) | 19 tok/s | 16 / 21; 5 of 13 clean units flagged; thinking on is unusable (447 s, then failed) |
174	| phi4-mini 3.8b (2.5 GB) | 100% | 24 tok/s | **Rejected:** 8 of its first 11 units wrong (flagged correct mappings), then stalled |
175	
176	### What affects speed and fit
177	| Lever | Effect |
178	|---|---|
179	| Free VRAM before loading | **Decisive**: fit or half-CPU is a 2x speed difference |
180	| Smaller `num_ctx` (2048 / 3072 / 4096) | Inconsistent fit results across runs; not a reliable lever |
181	| Flash attention + 8-bit KV cache (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`) | Same speed, but **2.9 GB instead of 3.2 GB**, so more headroom against other apps |
182	| Schema-constrained vs free JSON; CPU thread count | **No effect** (22.7 tok/s in every case; CPU idle) |
183	| "Keep the reason to 20 words" | 2.1x faster per unit (3.5 s) but **accuracy fell from 20/21 to 16/21**: the explanation helps the model. Do not shorten. |
184	| GPU clocks | Reaches its 6001 MHz memory clock and 1500 MHz core clock under load. Not stuck in a low power state. |
185	
186	**Ceiling: about 23 tokens/s for a 4B model on this card.** Faster needs a smaller model (a 1.7B download was started and cut off by the restart; not tested) or fewer output tokens. An 8B model (5.2 GB) cannot fit.
187	
188	### The finding that changes the design
189	**Not repeatable, even at temperature 0 with a fixed seed.** Run twice, `qwen3:4b-instruct` gave a different decision on 1 of 4 units: for JE-006 (the injection case) run 2 returned a degenerate repeated category list and `risk: false` while still listing "unbalanced". (`qwen3.5:4b` was identical on 3 of 3 units, so it varies by model.)
190	
191	Consequences, now part of the design:
192	1. **The ledger is the only source of determinism.** A local model can never be re-run to reproduce a result.
193	2. **Use one boolean per risk category, not a list.** Lists degenerate in constrained decoding.
194	3. **Derive `risk` in code** from the booleans. The model must not be able to say `risk: false` while flagging a category.
195	4. **The grounding verifier checks every claim separately**: for example "unbalanced" is checked against the actual debits and credits, and "exceeds balance" against the actual balance.
196	5. Keep the prompt version in the ledger key: small models are sensitive to wording.
197	
198	### Verdict
199	`qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` is a usable **free, offline second opinion for the scoped unit review (L3), behind the grounding verifier**: fast enough for a one-time recording run (about 100 units in 10 to 15 minutes), accurate on this set, and zero-cost. It is **not** the primary reviewer, not interactive, and not for long-context jobs. Sample size is small (21 units, my labels), so treat the numbers as indicative.
200	
201	**Where it earns its place:** development and the eval harness without an API key; live-session resilience (a changed input that misses the ledger can be answered on your laptop with no internet); and **model diversity** (a cloud model and a different-family local model agreeing is a stronger independent signal). The shipped ledger is recorded with the cloud model the eval selects.
202	
203	**Recommended local settings:** `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, `num_ctx` 4096, `num_predict` 400, temperature 0, fixed seed, full-length reasons.
204	
205	### Housekeeping
206	`phi4-mini` was rejected and removed. Installed now: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` (recommended) and your original `qwen3.5:4b`. The interrupted `qwen3:1.7b` download left a small partial file; that model was not tested.
207	
208	## 9. Logging, tracing and evals (decision)
209	
210	- **Audit lineage** is an output of the engine (origin rows, traces, manifest), not a tool. See `ARCHITECTURE_v2.md` section 16.
211	- **Run log:** stdlib `logging`, JSON lines per run in `.northwind/logs/`. No logging framework.
212	- **LLM observability:** the ledger. Optional OpenTelemetry export via PydanticAI instrumentation, off by default. The installed set contains only the OpenTelemetry **API**, with no exporter, so nothing leaves the machine unless an SDK and exporter are added deliberately.
213	- **Evals:** `pydantic-evals` (already pinned) with custom deterministic evaluators, run under pytest. An LLM-judge evaluator exists in the same package if narration ever needs one.

Nothing is committed or pushed yet. The pre-commit hook rejected the first commit, so I stopped at step 3.

**What I did**
- `python .agent/tools/make_manifest.py --check` prints "bundle intact".
- I created an empty `output/.gitkeep`, because git can't track an empty folder and `.gitignore` already expects that file.
- I staged exactly your list of paths, and the staged diff has 35 files. Nothing from `.agent/` or `.claude/` is in it.

**Why it stopped**

The pre-commit hook (`.agent/tools/githooks/pre_commit_check.py`) rejected five placeholder files that your list includes:
- `ledger/.gitkeep`
- `ledger/README.md`
- `output/.gitkeep`
- `transcripts/.gitkeep`
- `transcripts/README.md`

The hook allows only `.jsonl` files in `ledger/` and has no entry for `output/` or `transcripts/`. I wrote that allow-list in Step 0, before your instruction.

I tried to widen it for those paths, and the auto-mode permission classifier denied the edit because it changes a commit guardrail. That edit never ran, and I haven't used `--no-verify`.

**Your options**
1. **You widen the hook.** In `.agent/tools/githooks/pre_commit_check.py`, add `"output/"` and `"transcripts/"` to `ALLOWED_DIRS`. Also let `.gitkeep` and `README.md` pass the `ledger/` rule. Then copy the file to `.git/hooks/pre_commit_check.py`. I'll then retry the commit, push, and continue.
2. **Drop the placeholders.** I unstage those five files and commit the rest as "add assignment package and config". The `output/` and `transcripts/` folders won't exist in a fresh clone until a later commit adds files there.

**Two things to know**
- **Line endings:** Git warns it will convert LF to CRLF on Windows checkouts. That would change the data files' bytes and break the SHA-256 manifest in a fresh clone. I'll add a `.gitattributes` that keeps the data as LF in the tooling commit. I left it out of commit 1 because it isn't on your list.
- **Steps 4 to 9:** I haven't started them. They depend on commit 1 landing first, so the history reads in the order you specified.

import subprocess

REAL = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
results: list[tuple[str, bool, str]] = []


def check(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
    results.append((name, ok, detail))
    print(("PASS  " if ok else "FAIL  ") + name + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail and not ok else ""))


def run(cmd, cwd, stdin=None, **kw):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)


def hook(tmp: Path, script: str, payload: dict) -> tuple[int, dict | None, str]:
    out = run([sys.executable, str(tmp / ".claude/hooks" / script)], tmp, json.dumps(payload))
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(out.stdout) if out.stdout.strip() else None
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        parsed = None
    return out.returncode, parsed, out.stdout + out.stderr


def denied(parsed) -> bool:
    return bool(parsed) and parsed.get("hookSpecificOutput", {}).get("permissionDecision") == "deny"


def bash(tmp: Path, command: str):
    return hook(tmp, "guard_bash.py", {"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": command}})


def setup(tmp: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copytree(REAL / ".claude/hooks", tmp / ".claude/hooks", ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))

    for f in (REAL / ".agent/tools/githooks").iterdir():
        if f.is_file():
            shutil.copy(f, gh / f.name)
    (tmp / ".agent/STATE.md").write_text("# State\nNEXT: test\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (tmp / ".agent/WORKLOG.md").write_text("first\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (tmp / ".agent/TASKS.md").write_text("- [x] a\n- [ ] open task\n", encoding="utf-8")
    run(["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main"], tmp)
    run(["git", "config", "user.name", "T"], tmp)

    (tmp / "app").mkdir()
    (tmp / "app/x.py").write_text("x = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")

    check("2 normal commit passes, message only", r.returncode == 0 and msg.strip() == "add the first module", r.stderr)

"""Record or verify the SHA-256 of every supplied data file, so a test can prove the data was never edited.

The data stays in Northwind_TakeHome_v2/data (it is never copied); the manifest lives in config/.

Usage: python .agent/tools/make_manifest.py           (writes config/bundle_manifest.sha256)
       python .agent/tools/make_manifest.py --check   (verifies, exit 1 on any difference)
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA = ROOT / "Northwind_TakeHome_v2" / "data"
MANIFEST = ROOT / "config" / "bundle_manifest.sha256"


def compute() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(DATA.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    current = compute()
    if args.check:
        recorded = {name: digest for digest, name in (line.split("  ", 1) for line in MANIFEST.read_text().splitlines() if line)}
        bad = sorted(k for k in set(current) | set(recorded) if current.get(k) != recorded.get(k))
        for name in bad:
            print(f"MISMATCH: {name}")
        print("bundle intact" if not bad else f"{len(bad)} file(s) differ")
        return 1 if bad else 0
    MANIFEST.write_text("".join(f"{digest}  {name}\n" for name, digest in current.items()), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"wrote {MANIFEST} ({len(current)} files)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.content:
1	# Northwind Group consolidation
2	
3	Consolidates a three-entity, multi-currency group (a US parent, a UK subsidiary and an 80% Indian subsidiary) into GBP
4	for FY2024 and produces its statements. An AI review layer reads the data and **can only recommend**.
5	Assignment bundle ID **NWG-D0BC**.
6	
7	> **Status: structure and configuration only.** The application code is built wave by wave. The table at the end says
8	> exactly what exists.
9	
10	## Principles
11	
12	1. Every number on a statement is computed by deterministic code on `Decimal`. No model output is a number.
13	2. The AI layer recommends; a rule or a human decides. Free text in the data is quarantined and never obeyed.
14	3. A figure that cannot be determined is `null` with a reason. Nothing is estimated.
15	4. Every figure traces back to `file:line`. The same inputs give identical bytes.
16	
17	## Layout
18	
19	```
20	.
21	├── Northwind_TakeHome_v2/   the supplied assignment: brief PDF, its README, data/ (never edited)
22	├── app/                     the application
23	│   ├── main.py  routes.py  api_models.py  cli.py  config.py
24	│   ├── agents/              one folder per AI reviewer: llm_model.py  prompts.py  schema.py  tools.py
25	│   ├── orchestrator/        the LangGraph workflow
26	│   ├── llm/                 the only code that talks to a model provider
27	│   ├── review/              review units, evidence packets, grounding checks
28	│   ├── core/                the deterministic consolidation
29	│   ├── parsers/  detectors/  verification/  writers/  domain/
30	│   └── db/  services/  utils/
31	├── frontend/                review UI (plain static files)
32	├── tests/                   unit, golden, perturbation, property, red-team, eval and architecture tests
33	├── config/                  human-edited settings: policy, assumptions, overrides, llm; data checksums
34	├── ledger/                  recorded AI calls, one file per model
35	├── output/                  generated results
36	├── docs/                    the architecture document and the code guide
37	├── transcripts/             full AI session records
38	├── run.py                   one entry point: consolidate | serve | check
39	├── README.md  DECISIONS.md  VALIDATION.md  REFLECTION.md
40	└── pyproject.toml  requirements*.txt  .env.example  .gitignore  .github/
41	```

# Northwind Group consolidation

Consolidates a three-entity, multi-currency group (a US parent, a UK subsidiary and an 80% Indian subsidiary) into GBP
for FY2024 and produces its statements. An AI review layer reads the data and **can only recommend**.
Assignment bundle ID **NWG-D0BC**.

> **Status: structure and configuration only.** The application code is built wave by wave. The table at the end says
> exactly what exists.

## Principles

1. Every number on a statement is computed by deterministic code on `Decimal`. No model output is a number.
2. The AI layer recommends; a rule or a human decides. Free text in the data is quarantined and never obeyed.
3. A figure that cannot be determined is `null` with a reason. Nothing is estimated.
4. Every figure traces back to `file:line`. The same inputs give identical bytes.

## Layout

```
.
├── Northwind_TakeHome_v2/   the supplied assignment: brief PDF, its README, data/ (never edited)
├── app/                     the application
│   ├── main.py  routes.py  api_models.py  cli.py  config.py
│   ├── agents/              one folder per AI reviewer: llm_model.py  prompts.py  schema.py  tools.py
│   ├── orchestrator/        the LangGraph workflow
│   ├── llm/                 the only code that talks to a model provider
│   ├── review/              review units, evidence packets, grounding checks
│   ├── core/                the deterministic consolidation
│   ├── parsers/  detectors/  verification/  writers/  domain/
│   └── db/  services/  utils/
├── frontend/                review UI (plain static files)
├── tests/                   unit, golden, perturbation, property, red-team, eval and architecture tests
├── config/                  human-edited settings: policy, assumptions, overrides, llm; data checksums
├── ledger/                  recorded AI calls, one file per model
├── output/                  generated results
├── docs/                    the architecture document and the code guide
├── transcripts/             full AI session records
├── run.py                   one entry point: consolidate | serve | check
├── README.md  DECISIONS.md  VALIDATION.md  REFLECTION.md
└── pyproject.toml  requirements*.txt  .env.example  .gitignore  .github/
```

**The AI is kept away from the numbers by structure.** The folders that produce or touch a number (`core`, `parsers`,
`detectors`, `verification`, `writers`, `domain`) never import AI or web code, agents never import `core`, and only
`app/llm/` imports a model library. `tests/test_architecture.py` enforces it.

```bash
python -m venv .venv

```

```bash
python run.py consolidate     # the one command: reads Northwind_TakeHome_v2/data/, writes output/
python run.py serve           # API and review UI on http://127.0.0.1:8000
python run.py check           # environment, data integrity, config
```

Set `model` in `config/llm.toml`, or the `NORTHWIND_MODEL` environment variable. Strings: `ollama:<model>`,

12 control figures are identical whichever model is used, and a test enforces it.

# Code guide

A plain-English guide to the repository. It describes what exists now; each wave adds to it.
Current state: **Wave 0 done** (structure, tooling, guard tests). No consolidation logic yet.

## Run and test

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest
python -m ruff check .
python -m mypy app
python run.py consolidate         # prints "not built yet (Wave 1)" and exits 2
```

## What each top-level folder is for

| Folder | Role |
|---|---|
| `Northwind_TakeHome_v2/` | The supplied brief and data. Never edited. |
| `app/` | The application. Every file is a docstring-only shell until its wave. |
| `config/` | Hand-edited TOML settings, and `bundle_manifest.sha256`, the SHA-256 of each supplied data file. |
| `tests/` | `test_structure`, `test_architecture` and `test_bundle` today; unit, golden, perturbation, property, red-team and eval folders later. |
| `ledger/`, `output/`, `transcripts/` | Recorded AI calls, generated results and AI session records. Empty for now. |

## How `app/` is divided

The split exists to keep AI output away from numbers.

- `core`, `parsers`, `detectors`, `verification`, `writers`, `domain` touch numbers. They import no AI, web or
  model code.
- `agents` hold AI reviewers. They never import `core`, so a reviewer can read evidence but cannot calculate.
- `llm` is the only place that imports a model library.
- `db` is the only place that uses `sqlite3`.

`tests/test_architecture.py` reads every source file with Python's `ast` module and fails if one of these rules is
broken. It also tests its own checker on small snippets, so it cannot pass by checking nothing.

## What the three tests prove

- `test_structure.py`: `app/` contains exactly the files in the structure plan (no missing, no extra), every folder is
  a package, each full agent folder has its four files, the stretch agents have only `__init__.py`.
- `test_architecture.py`: the import rules above.
- `test_bundle.py`: the 15 supplied data files hash to the values in `config/bundle_manifest.sha256`. In a fresh clone
  this checks the committed bytes, because `.gitattributes` stops git from changing line endings in the data folder.

## Choices worth explaining

- **Pinned requirements.** Exact versions, so a fresh clone installs what was tested. Pins were checked against PyPI
  on 2026-11-17. `google-genai` is left unpinned until Gemini is first used.
- **TOML for config.** YAML reads `0031` as the number 25; TOML refuses it.
- **No line-ending conversion for the data.** The first commit stored 12 CSV files with changed line endings; the
  second commit corrected it and is recorded in `VALIDATION.md`.

# Code guide

A plain-English guide to the repository. It describes what exists now; each wave adds to it.
Current state: **Wave 0 done** (structure, tooling, guard tests). No consolidation logic yet.

## Run and test

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest
python -m ruff check .
python -m mypy app
python run.py consolidate         # prints "not built yet (Wave 1)" and exits 2
```

## What each top-level folder is for

| Folder | Role |
|---|---|
| `Northwind_TakeHome_v2/` | The supplied brief and data. Never edited. |
| `app/` | The application. Every file is a docstring-only shell until its wave. |
| `config/` | Hand-edited TOML settings, and `bundle_manifest.sha256`, the SHA-256 of each supplied data file. |
| `tests/` | `test_structure`, `test_architecture` and `test_bundle` today; unit, golden, perturbation, property, red-team and eval folders later. |
| `ledger/`, `output/`, `transcripts/` | Recorded AI calls, generated results and AI session records. Empty for now. |

## How `app/` is divided

The split exists to keep AI output away from numbers.

- `core`, `parsers`, `detectors`, `verification`, `writers`, `domain` touch numbers. They import no AI, web or
  model code.
- `agents` hold AI reviewers. They never import `core`, so a reviewer can read evidence but cannot calculate.
- `llm` is the only place that imports a model library.
- `db` is the only place that uses `sqlite3`.

`tests/test_architecture.py` reads every source file with Python's `ast` module and fails if one of these rules is
broken. It also tests its own checker on small snippets, so it cannot pass by checking nothing.

- `test_bundle.py`: the 15 supplied data files hash to the values in `config/bundle_manifest.sha256`. In a fresh clone
  this checks the committed bytes, because `.gitattributes` stops git from changing line endings in the data folder.

43	## 6. Code and writing style (humans must believe a human wrote it)
44	- Small functions, plain names, type hints, short docstrings. Files under about 200 lines. No dead code, no commented-out code, no TODO litter.
45	- Comments explain **why** and cite the rule: `# policy 3: foreign-currency items are restated at the closing rate`. Never narrate what the next line does. No banner comments, no emoji, no "robust/seamless/leverage" language.
46	- Money is `Decimal` from strings, never float. Account codes are text. Round only at output.
47	- Tests read like a person wrote them: one behaviour each, a clear name, real numbers from the data.
48	- Follow `PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md` and its import rules exactly. Add `tests/test_architecture.py` early.
49	
50	## 7. Commits: automatic, small, human, clean
51	- Commit once per finished task in TASKS.md (a module with its tests and its CODE_GUIDE entry), never per small edit. Expect roughly 20 to 40 commits for the whole build. A task is finished only when ruff, mypy and pytest are green and you have read `git diff --cached`. One logical change per commit.
52	- Review gate: when a wave's goal is met, write `.agent/REVIEW_wave<N>.md` (what changed, the files to read first, the figures and the assumptions that moved, anything you are unsure of), push, and stop. The user reads the diff and replies before the next wave starts. Never begin the next wave on your own.
53	- Message: **one line, at most two**. Lowercase, imperative, plain. About 60 characters on line one; line two only if the why is not obvious. Good: `translate india p&l at the h2 average rate`. Good: `reject unbalanced journals before posting`. Bad: `feat: implement comprehensive translation module`.
54	- **No trailers of any kind.** No Co-Authored-By, no session links, no mention of any AI or tool.
55	- Stage explicit paths only: `git add path/one path/two`. **Never** `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit -a`. Before every commit run `git status --short` and `git diff --cached --stat`, and read them.
56	- Only necessary files. Never commit: `.agent/`, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE*.md`, `.env`, `.venv/`, `.northwind/`, caches, logs, `*.db`, scratch files, generated `output/` (until the final reviewed sample).
57	- Never amend, rebase, reset history, or force-push. The brief needs the full history. Fix mistakes with a new commit.
58	- Never use `--no-verify`: the commit-msg hook strips tool trailers and enforces the message style. After the first push and after each wave, check the pushed history: `git log --format=%B origin/main | grep -i -E "claude|anthropic|co-authored"` must print nothing.
59	- Use the repository's configured git identity. Do not set `--author`.
60	- Push to `origin main` at the end of each wave and when stopping. If a push fails, log it and continue.

# Code guide

A plain-English guide to the repository. It describes what exists now; each wave adds to it.
Current state: **Wave 0 done** (structure, tooling, guard tests). No consolidation logic yet.

## Run and test

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest
python -m ruff check .
python -m mypy app
python run.py consolidate         # prints "not built yet (Wave 1)" and exits 2
```

## What each top-level folder is for

| Folder | Role |
|---|---|
| `Northwind_TakeHome_v2/` | The supplied brief and data. Never edited. |
| `app/` | The application. Every file is a docstring-only shell until its wave. |
| `config/` | Hand-edited TOML settings, and `bundle_manifest.sha256`, the SHA-256 of each supplied data file. |
| `tests/` | `test_structure`, `test_architecture` and `test_bundle` today; unit, golden, perturbation, property, red-team and eval folders later. |
| `ledger/`, `output/`, `transcripts/` | Recorded AI calls, generated results and AI session records. Empty for now. |

## How `app/` is divided

The split exists to keep AI output away from numbers.

- `core`, `parsers`, `detectors`, `verification`, `writers`, `domain` touch numbers. They import no AI, web or
  model code.
- `agents` hold AI reviewers. They never import `core`, so a reviewer can read evidence but cannot calculate.
- `llm` is the only place that imports a model library.
- `db` is the only place that uses `sqlite3`.

`tests/test_architecture.py` reads every source file with Python's `ast` module and fails if one of these rules is
broken. It also tests its own checker on small snippets, so it cannot pass by checking nothing.

## What the three tests prove

- `test_structure.py`: `app/` contains exactly the files in the structure plan (no missing, no extra), every folder is
  a package, each full agent folder has its four files, the stretch agents have only `__init__.py`.
- `test_architecture.py`: the import rules above.
- `test_bundle.py`: the 15 supplied data files hash to the values in `config/bundle_manifest.sha256`. In a fresh clone
  this checks the committed bytes, because `.gitattributes` stops git from changing line endings in the data folder.

## Choices worth explaining

- **Pinned requirements.** Exact versions, so a fresh clone installs what was tested. Pins were checked against PyPI
  on 2026-11-17. `google-genai` is left unpinned until Gemini is first used.
- **TOML for config.** YAML reads `0031` as the number 25; TOML refuses it.
- **No line-ending conversion for the data.** The first commit stored 12 CSV files with changed line endings; the
  second commit ("store data files byte for byte") corrected it.

# Northwind Group - accounting policies for consolidation (FY2024)

1. **Presentation currency.** The group presents its consolidated statements in GBP.
2. **Translation of entity statements into GBP.**
   - Assets and liabilities: closing rate at 31 December 2024.
   - Income and expenses: average rate for the period in which they are included in the group.
     For the US, the FY2024 average. For India, the H2 (1 July to 31 December 2024) average.
   - Equity: historical rates. Opening group equity is given in `prior_year_group.csv`.
   - Exchange differences on translation go to the translation reserve (account 3300).
   - Where a GBP rate is not given directly, use the product of the two given rates of the same type
     (for example, GBP/INR closing = GBP/USD closing x USD/INR closing).
3. **Foreign currency items inside an entity's own books.** Monetary items in a currency other than the
   entity's functional currency are retranslated at the closing rate. Differences go to profit or loss
   (group account 7300).
4. **Business combinations.** Non-controlling interest is measured at its proportionate share of net assets.
   Goodwill is held in the subsidiary's functional currency and retranslated at the closing rate.
5. **Intercompany.** Intercompany balances, income and expenses are eliminated in full. Items in transit
   at the year end are recorded by the receiving entity at the closing rate. Any remaining exchange
   difference on eliminating intercompany income and expense goes to group account 7300.
6. **Journals.** Manual journals are posted only if they are valid for FY2024. Invalid journals are not posted.
7. **Rounding.** Translate at full precision and round each reported figure to 2 decimal places.

1	# Northwind Group - accounting policies for consolidation (FY2024)
2	
3	1. **Presentation currency.** The group presents its consolidated statements in GBP.
4	2. **Translation of entity statements into GBP.**
5	   - Assets and liabilities: closing rate at 31 December 2024.
6	   - Income and expenses: average rate for the period in which they are included in the group.
7	     For the US, the FY2024 average. For India, the H2 (1 July to 31 December 2024) average.
8	   - Equity: historical rates. Opening group equity is given in `prior_year_group.csv`.
9	   - Exchange differences on translation go to the translation reserve (account 3300).
10	   - Where a GBP rate is not given directly, use the product of the two given rates of the same type
11	     (for example, GBP/INR closing = GBP/USD closing x USD/INR closing).
12	3. **Foreign currency items inside an entity's own books.** Monetary items in a currency other than the
13	   entity's functional currency are retranslated at the closing rate. Differences go to profit or loss
14	   (group account 7300).
15	4. **Business combinations.** Non-controlling interest is measured at its proportionate share of net assets.
16	   Goodwill is held in the subsidiary's functional currency and retranslated at the closing rate.
17	5. **Intercompany.** Intercompany balances, income and expenses are eliminated in full. Items in transit
18	   at the year end are recorded by the receiving entity at the closing rate. Any remaining exchange
19	   difference on eliminating intercompany income and expense goes to group account 7300.
20	6. **Journals.** Manual journals are posted only if they are valid for FY2024. Invalid journals are not posted.
21	7. **Rounding.** Translate at full precision and round each reported figure to 2 decimal places.

# Hand calculation v0 (provisional golden figures)

Produced by `handcalc_v0.py` (throwaway, Decimal, full precision, rounded at print). **Written by the AI assistant, not yet reviewed by a human.** Treat as the first independent check, not as truth.

## Assumptions baked in (each is an open item for DECISIONS.md or an email)
A1. The 20 journals are **not** already in the TBs.
A2. Dispositions: post 15 (001-005, 007, 008, 010-015, 018, 020), reject 3 (006 unbalanced, 017 dated 2025, 019 duplicate of 014), hold 2 (009 exceeds balance, 016 unknown account).
A3. UK `2310` remapped to group `2300` (deferred income is a liability). As supplied it would add 180,000 to UK revenue and profit.
A4. India journals dated 31 Dec are post-acquisition, so they reduce Jul-Dec profit (42,000,000 -> 32,800,000 INR). No tax is booked on them.
A5. UK in-transit invoice booked at closing (policy 5); UK USD payable revalued at closing (policy 3); residual of income vs expense elimination to 7300.
A6. SGD bank carried at its booked 23,010 inside total assets (no closing rate exists).
A7. NCI proportionate (policy 4): NCI = 20% of India net assets (excluding goodwill) at the closing rate.

## Figures

| Key | Value (GBP) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| group_revenue | 28,301,607.81 | determined (given A1-A3) |
| group_profit | 2,768,780.95 | determined |
| profit_owners | 2,707,922.89 | determined |
| profit_nci | 60,858.06 | determined |
| nci_closing | 1,325,107.53 | determined (acq 1,285,958.29 + profit 60,858.06 + translation -21,708.82) |
| goodwill_closing | 1,375,815.07 | determined (INR 147,600,000 at closing) |
| translation_reserve_movement | 43,706.74 | determined (closing 456,056.74 vs opening 412,350.00) |
| total_assets | 28,575,272.95 | **provisional**: includes SGD bank at booked 23,010 |
| total_equity | 18,343,835.08 | determined |
| intercompany_difference | 20,066.42 = 8,108.54 in transit + 11,957.88 revaluation | determined; plus 1,966.21 P&L rate residual to 7300 |
| sgd_bank_gbp | **null** | no GBP/SGD closing rate |
| journals | posted 15 / rejected 3 / held 2 | judgment calls noted in A2 |

## Cross-check
Reserve movement by **balance route** (equity as net assets minus share capital, retained earnings, NCI) and by **components route** (US opening net assets +201,488.13; US profit +28,979.74; India net assets and profit, owners 80% -86,835.30; India goodwill -23,944.83; UK investment retranslation removed -15,924.08; India investment retranslation removed -60,056.92) agree to **0.007**. The gap is consistent with the cent-rounding in the supplied opening equity (`prior_year_group.csv` ties to the unrounded opening equity within 0.004). The oracle's tolerance for this check must be set explicitly (0.01), not left implicit.

## What this showed
Total equity is fixed by net assets, NCI is fixed by the proportionate method, and retained earnings by opening RE plus owners' profit, so the reserve is determinate. The treatment chosen for eliminating the investments changes only how the reserve decomposes, not any control figure. Only `sgd_bank_gbp` is a true null.

## Sensitivities to quote when an item is overridden
- JE-017 posted instead of rejected: revenue falls by about 17,214.40 (22,000 USD at the average rate).
- UK `2310` left mapped to `4100`: revenue and profit rise by 180,000.00.
- JE-018 / JE-020 treated as already booked: India Jul-Dec profit rises by (2,700,000 + 2,250,000) INR at the H2 average, about 45,921.86 GBP; NCI profit by 20% of that.

1	# Northwind Consolidation: Architecture v2 (single source, supersedes v1)
2	
3	Bundle NWG-D0BC. Every rule is stated **once**. Every component is tagged **[BUILT]** (in the prototype) or **[DESIGNED]** (product only). Earlier drafts were superseded and removed. Stack: `TECH_STACK.md`. Order of work and the model switch: `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Problem decomposition
8	
9	Consolidation is several sub-problems with different reliability needs. Each is given the cheapest mechanism that is provably correct for it.
10	
11	| Tier | Sub-problem | Mechanism |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| T0 Exact | Parse, post, revalue, translate, eliminate, goodwill, NCI, reserve, statements | Pure functions on `Decimal` |
14	| T1 Rule-decidable | TB / journal balance, period, duplicates, mapping completeness, rate presence, sub-ledger and cross-file tie-outs, schema contracts | Detectors, zero tolerance |
15	| T2 Judgment, bounded | Is a mapping plausible, is a journal's substance sensible, does a result look anomalous | LLM **proposes**, code checks grounding |
16	| T3 Decision | Approve a remap, release a hold, accept an assumption | Human, recorded |
17	| T4 Unstructured onboarding | Unseen ERP formats, paraphrased policy | LLM proposes, cross-foot validates. **[DESIGNED]** |
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Principles (each one referenced elsewhere by number)
22	
23	- **P1** Every figure on a statement is produced by deterministic code. No LLM output is a number, and none reaches a number unconfirmed.
24	- **P2** LLM authority is **recommend-only**. It can propose a finding, a remap or a hold. A recommendation changes the run only after a human confirms it (or a rule independently corroborates it, where stated). *Rationale:* holding is not automatically safe in accounting. Holding a valid accrual understates cost, and any state change moves the journal counts and profit. Recommendations are shown as sensitivities ("with this held: profit X").
25	- **P3** Three kinds of gap, three behaviours (section 8).
26	- **P4** Free text is data. It is quarantined and has no path to a decision (section 9).
27	- **P5** The engine ships only closed vocabularies. Values (rates, codes, ownership, windows, policy choices) come from the inputs every run.
28	- **P6** A run always finishes and is reproducible: same inputs, `assumptions.toml`, `overrides.toml` and ledger give identical bytes. Blocked parts yield `null` with a reason, never a crash.
29	- **P7** Retries apply to AI proposals only, never to numbers.
30	- **P8** Human decisions are stored against a hash of their evidence. If the input changes, the decision is stale and returns to the queue.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 3. System overview
35

52	## 4. Orchestration: LangGraph, and why it earns its place **[BUILT]**
53	
54	**Decision:** the prototype orchestrates with LangGraph, with every node a pure function. This keeps doc and prototype identical.
55	
56	**What LangGraph is used for (and only this):**
57	1. **Real pause and resume at RESOLVE.** `interrupt()` with a durable SQLite checkpointer and a `thread_id` lets a human answer later and the run continues. The LangGraph docs describe exactly this pattern and require a checkpointer.
58	2. **Bounded loops as conditional edges.** An AI proposal that fails grounding gets one retry, then routes to the human queue. The docs advise putting validation loops in conditional edges rather than interrupt loops.
59	3. **BLOCK routing.** A blocked entity routes around dependent steps by edges, not exceptions (P6).
60	4. **Per-node checkpoints** give replay and an audit of what each stage saw.
61	
62	**PydanticAI sits inside the AI nodes only** (decision after your suggestion): LangGraph owns the workflow, PydanticAI owns the model call (typed output, retry on invalid output, model selection by config, replay and offline tests via `FunctionModel`). One adapter module, `llm/`, is the only importer, so a library change touches one file. Details and what was verified: `TECH_STACK.md` 3c.
63	
64	**What it is not used for:** no node chooses the next node by LLM, no multi-agent handoffs, no numbers inside graph machinery. The graph is static. The only agent-like parts are the L2 and L3 reviewers, and they run inside single nodes.
65	
66	**Design rule: state carries pointers, not payloads.** The graph state holds `run_id`, input hashes, stage status, open item keys and artifact references. All tables and `Decimal` values live in the SQLite evidence store and are read by exact query. A spike showed `Decimal` round-trips exactly through the SQLite checkpoint, so this is no longer a serialisation risk. Pointer-state stays for size, one auditable store of record, and exact queries.
67	
68	**Safety net:** a plain runner calls the same node functions in order. A test asserts both runners produce identical output hashes. If a fresh-clone install of LangGraph fails on a reviewer's machine, `--engine plain` produces the same bytes. The spike was run (see `TECH_STACK.md` section 4): interrupt, then resume in a separate process, passed on this machine.
69	
70	**Honest limit for the doc:** LangGraph contributes durability, resumability and routing. It contributes nothing to numerical correctness. That comes from P1 and section 7.

102	### 6.1 Ingest and L1 inline scanners **[BUILT]**
103	- One adapter per layout (debit/credit columns; signed balance; amount + Dr/Cr), chosen from the header. Unknown header means BLOCK that entity.
104	- **Schema contract per file** (columns, types, allowed values). A violation is BLOCK with file, line, reason.
105	- Codes are text. `0031` never becomes `31`. Only outer whitespace is trimmed. A match that needs further normalising is a proposal, not an applied match.
106	- Free text goes to the quarantine type at the door.
